summary: Feed s108_single is degraded: NDR requires bidirectional traffic but 73.5% of TCP sessions (147/200) are one-way only. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is delivering only one direction for most flows. 147 of 200 TCP sessions show traffic in a single direction (73.5% vs 10% threshold), typical of a SPAN port configured with 'rx' or 'tx' only, a single-sided TAP, or a broker policy that forwards only one side of an asymmetric path without bidirectional aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions for TCP handshake/reassembly, state tracking, and anomaly detection. With 73.5% one-way sessions the NDR cannot reconstruct flows, will miss lateral movement, C2, data exfiltration and generate false negatives/incomplete session records.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow (client->server and server->client) to the same NDR tool port, or replace unidirectional SPAN with dual-direction TAP aggregation, so NDR receives complete bidirectional sessions for detection.
